## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `0bbcdd99620428615efe52db34e6981faf46498c`
Local-runs: none
Scope: packages/metadata-protocol/src/protocol-write-face.ts, packages/objectql/src/protocol-destructive-currency-mode.test.ts (`reviewFace` hits: none; these two are the narrowing-face floor, every diff path outside the prose faces) + packages/metadata-protocol/src/protocol-save.ts (the Phase 3a-destructive gate and its `force`), packages/objectql/src/validation/record-currency-code.ts (`recordCurrencyFieldOf`), packages/spec/src/data/field.zod.ts (`refuseRecordModeKeyMismatch`, `homeAmount`), packages/cli/src/commands/migrate/record-currency-codes.ts and recompute-home-amounts.ts, packages/rest/src/meta-record-currency-backfill-route.ts, docs/adr/0144 D2 and D5 (all read in the live tree, none reviewed)

Inputs: card #31949 (body, triage 6743182628, claim 6744531721, os-dev-report 6747960601), PR #31969 body, file list and net diff against `main` at `0cd594b3` (the merge base is `origin/main` itself), and the 49 check-runs on `0bbcdd99`: 36 `success`, 13 `skipped`, 0 failed, so every derived gate family on this head is green. Changeset, docs prose and lockfiles are not reviewed; the PR body's account is not evidence.

### ① Derived judgments

- **Accept set, judged right as a narrowing of exactly one transition.** In `detectDestructiveObjectChanges` the new branch fires only when `recordCurrencyPointerOf(prevField)` and `recordCurrencyPointerOf(nextField)` are both defined (both sides `type: 'currency'`, `currencyMode: 'record'`, a non-empty string `currencyField`), differ as written, and `isStored(prevField)`. So a save of an `object` whose stored record-mode amount now names another pointer answers the existing 409 `DESTRUCTIVE_CHANGE` unless `request.force`. No other save moves: a mode switch into `record` has no previous pointer and raises only the sibling (`prevField.currencyConfig?.currencyMode !== 'record'` and `prevPointer === undefined` are the same fact, so the two branches are exclusive); leaving record mode, a new object (`host.readMetaItem` finds no `prev`, the gate is skipped before any finding), a new field (`if (!prevField) continue`), a formula previous field (no pointer, and `isStored` false), and an identical pointer all raise nothing, as before. The gate runs only for `singularType === 'object'` and only without `force`, unchanged.
- **Reads no row.** The branch reads `prev`/`next` field declarations only; the one row count in this gate (`withNullMasterRowCounts`) is keyed on `field_required_no_default` findings of `controlled_by_parent` masters and never on this code. Right.
- **`force` escape, judged right and inherited whole.** `protocol-save.ts` L1055 skips the whole gate on `request.force`; the REST `PUT /api/v1/meta/:type/:name` door threads `?force`. The remedy clause appended to the 409 message is `destructiveChangeRemedy(request.writeFace, name)`, which on the `meta-dispatch`, `package-duplicate`, `external-import` and `package-unmanaged-import` faces says the door accepts no `force`. The new finding changes nothing about that: it is one more finding in a gate whose per-face lift was ruled on #11095 and commit 82cb6e849, and the sibling `currency_mode_to_record` sits on the same faces today.
- **Public surface: one new wire value.** `issues[].code` on the 409 envelope gains `currency_field_repointed`. That is a new member of the destructive-finding vocabulary a consumer may switch on — the same kind of addition the precedent a3d24c9 declared for `currency_mode_to_record` (its PR declared `Clause-②: yes (widening)`, naming the new finding among the widenings). No authorable key, value, enum member or schema moves; `packages/spec` is untouched.
- **`currency_mode_to_record` message byte-identical.** Verified by reading: the four removed string fragments and `recordCurrencyCodeBackfillRemedy(objectName, fname)` concatenate to the same text, character for character, and `objectName` is hoisted with the same expression. The existing pins in the same file are unchanged in the diff.
- **Message claims against the live tree.** `os migrate record-currency-codes` and `os migrate recompute-home-amounts` exist (`packages/cli/src/commands/migrate/`); `POST /api/v1/meta/_migrate-record-currency-codes` exists (`packages/rest/src/meta-record-currency-backfill-route.ts`); no REST door for the recompute exists anywhere under `packages/`, so "a shell command, with no REST door" is true. A path target stores no code on the child (ADR-0144 D2 amendment, "The child stores no code of its own"), so withholding the backfill there is right. `homeAmountPointersOf` reads `homeAmount.field` and `homeAmount.rateField`, both required strings in `field.zod.ts`. "As written" comparison matches `recordCurrencyFieldOf`, which neither trims nor folds.
- **Tests pin it.** Eleven cases in the existing harness cover the four directions, backfill named or withheld, both home-amount clauses, `force`, identical pointers, no previous version, a former formula, and mode-switch exclusivity; the 409 envelope is asserted on `code`, `status` and the finding. `Test Core` 1–8 and the aggregate are `success` on this head.
- **Docs.** The new subsection in `content/docs/data-modeling/currency.mdx` names `?force=true` on `PUT /api/v1/meta/:type/:name` (the one door that reads it) and links `#recomputing-stored-home-amounts`, a heading that exists on `main` (L350). Prose face, not reviewed further.

### ② Semver level

- **Changeset: `@objectstack/metadata-protocol: patch`, `Metadata-protocol: none`.** Right under ruling A and the precedent: nothing an author writes against is added, removed or re-meant, and the value is not refused outright on the REST door, it is acknowledged with `force`. `check-changeset-no-major` would grade `none` + `patch` the same way beside a `(narrowing)` arm ("a non-protocol change, widening or breaking, ships `patch`"), so the kind does not have to move to repair the item below.
- **`Clause-②:` line — MUST-FIX.** Asked by the brief: does `no (a narrowing: …)` grade as the narrowing arm or as malformed? Neither. `readClause2Line` (the fleet's one reader) returns `{ kind: 'declared', value: 'no', arm: null }` on both the changeset body and the PR body. `readArmToken` reads the arm as the FIRST token inside the parenthesis, and its near-miss detector tests only that first word against `/widen|narrow/i`; the first word here is `a`, so the parenthetical is classed as ordinary reasoning and the line declares NO DIRECTION. The consequences on this head are the defect #16421 exists to remove: `reviewFace` on the committed paths plus both declarations answers `face: 'declaration', tierName: 'TIER_DEFAULT'`; `check-adr-0087-registration`'s `breakingDeclaration` collects no signal (no `major`, no `**BREAKING`, no `!`, no arm, no `narrowed`) and asks for no ADR-0087 disposition; the queue guard owes this PR no CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER record. The tree's own changeset body, the card, the claim and the PR all call the change a narrowing (200 → 409 without `force`), and the ruling that hangs the narrowing face is "exact like the other three" on the one spelling `Clause-②: no (narrowing)`. A changeset that reads as no direction for a change everyone party to it calls breaking is a contract-level defect of the declaration carrier in the tree, so it is graded must-fix, not should-fix. Fix: in `.changeset/31949-currency-field-repointed.md` and the PR body, spell `Clause-②: no (narrowing — a save that answered 200 now answers 409 without \`force\`; …)` (the arm word first inside the parenthesis; a `yes (narrowing)` is also admissible if the dev counts the new finding code as a widening, as a3d24c9 did), then add the ADR-0087 disposition marker the arm makes `check:adr-0087-registration` ask for (the gate prints the closed set), and re-measure `pnpm check:adr-0087-registration` and `check-changeset-no-major` on the new head. The edit moves the head; this record does not cover the fixed head, which will then derive the narrowing face at CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER and owes its delta review there.
- `Skills-docs: none` — right as far as the tree shows: no file under `skills/` or `.claude/skills/` names `currency_mode_to_record` or re-pointing, and `skills/objectstack-data/rules/field-types.md` teaches only the switch-into-record backfill, which stays true.

### ③ Boundary flags

- **Face/tier.** The brief orders CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER on the narrowing face; the recogniser, handed the committed paths and both declaration texts, derives the declaration face (TIER_DEFAULT) on this head because of the arm defect above. `Served-tier` here names the tier that in fact served this round, which is CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER (`scripts/pm/dispatch-gates.mjs` L12807), and is not restated as TIER_DEFAULT: that line is a provenance fact, not a face reading. On this head `servedTierStands` would not stand it on the derived face; on the fixed head the face is narrowing and the tier is exact. Flagged, not hidden.
- **Dev deviation 1** ("Clause-② line copied verbatim from the claim"): the claim's own spelling carried the defect, so the dev inherited it from the dispatching seat. Answered by the must-fix above; the seat's claim template should carry `no (narrowing — …)` from here on.
- **Dev deviation 2** (one failed relay `pr_create` run with no write): no trace in the tree or on the PR; nothing to answer.
- **`adr_note`** ("Seat may judge whether ADR-0144 D5 owes a line"): yes. The code comment cites "[ADR-0144 D2, D5]" as authority for a finding neither decision states; D5 says stored rows change only through an explicit recompute and the D2 amendment locks a parent's code once children follow it, but nothing on `main` speaks to re-pointing `currencyField`. Tier H: the seat files a follow-up card for a dated note under D5 (or D2) naming `currency_field_repointed`. Not blocking this PR, which was scoped away from `docs/adr/**`.
- **`out_of_scope_findings`** (recompute lists a path-following child's rows `code_blank` until #31911): confirmed as a reading of `recordCurrencyFieldOf`, which returns the two-segment pointer as a sibling column name. So the message's recompute prescription for a path target with `homeAmount` names a command that does not yet work for that shape. Carrier #31911; accepted deviation here, see ④ nit.
- **Dogfood battery**: the dev report waives it because the arm read null. Once the arm is spelled, the dev re-measures whether its dispatch rule owes the battery on a declared narrowing; this record does not assert either way.
- `open_questions: []`, `security_findings: none` — nothing to answer.

### ④ Design judgment

The narrowing read against the published spec on `main`, trying to break it:

- **Declared capability or spec's own refusal?** Neither, and that is the honest reading. ADR-0144 D2 declares what `currencyField` may name (a sibling code field; since the #31743 amendment a `master_detail.code` path). It declares no capability to re-point a stored field silently, and no refusal of re-pointing either. D5's rule — stored home amounts and rates change only through an explicit recompute — and the D2 lock on a parent's code are both there to stop a relabel without a re-rate, and a re-point is exactly that relabel at the metadata layer. The finding therefore takes nothing a consumer was promised away (the save still lands with `force` on the REST door, and the code still parses unchanged), and it does not make a spec refusal real (the spec has none), so it is a new gate in the same family as `field_type_change` and `field_required_no_default`, which the spec is also silent on. Not an implementation gap narrowed at the consumer: the capability is delivered. The ADR owes the note flagged in ③.
- **Attempts to break it.** (a) Both branches at once: impossible, shown in ①. (b) `fixed`/`dynamic` → `record` with a pointer: only the sibling fires, pinned. (c) `record` → `record` where the previous `currencyField` was `''`: the spec refuses that declaration at parse, and `recordCurrencyPointerOf` returns undefined for it anyway, so no false finding. (d) Prev `homeAmount` present, next adds a different `homeAmount.field`: the message names the OLD stored columns (`prevHome`) and the recompute, which is the right pair, since those are the rows that were converted. (e) Prev had no `homeAmount`, next adds one with the re-point: no home clause, correct, nothing stored to re-rate. (f) `isStored(prevField)` on a `currency` field is true (`isVirtualSearchField` is the spec's storage predicate), so an in-table amount is always judged; a prior formula is not. (g) Pointer with surrounding whitespace: compares as another field, as the PR says; the spec's `refuseDishonestRecordCurrencyField` refuses a pointer naming no code field earlier in the save, so the destructive finding is reached only for a pointer the schema admits. (h) Faces without `force`: on the dispatcher `PUT /meta`, duplicate, external-import and unmanaged-import doors a re-point is now refused with a remedy that says the door accepts no `force`; this is the gate's ruled face design, identical for every finding in it, and the REST `PUT` door remains the place a destructive change is acknowledged on purpose. No new hole opened.
- **Nit** — the changeset body says the save "(REST `PUT /meta`, Studio, a package publish)" answers 409 and "Re-submit with `force` to save"; `PUT /meta` is the dispatcher door that accepts no `force` (`destructiveChangeRemedy`, `meta-dispatch`), and the unmanaged import accepts none either. The docs page gets this right by naming `?force=true` on `PUT /api/v1/meta/:type/:name`. Prose; fold into the changeset edit the must-fix already makes.
- **Nit** — for a path target that declares `homeAmount`, the message prescribes `os migrate recompute-home-amounts`, which on `main` reports such rows `code_blank` until #31911 lands. The command is the one recompute that exists and ADR-0144 D5 says to name existing means, so the text is right in principle; accepted deviation with carrier #31911, no edit here.
- **Nit** — `objectName` hoisted above the first branch so both can read it; no behaviour change.
- No should-fix. The one must-fix is item ②'s declaration carrier, which decides the verdict.

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `f9675566b7b5e64d3ce9b37acf6b2cc8b819d720`

Scope: packages/metadata-protocol/src/protocol-write-face.ts, packages/objectql/src/protocol-destructive-currency-mode.test.ts (`reviewFace` hits: none; these two are the narrowing-face floor, every diff path outside the prose faces) + packages/metadata-protocol/src/protocol-save.ts (the Phase 3a-destructive gate and its `force`), packages/objectql/src/validation/record-currency-code.ts, packages/spec/src/data/field.zod.ts, packages/cli/src/commands/migrate/record-currency-codes.ts and recompute-home-amounts.ts, packages/rest/src/meta-record-currency-backfill-route.ts, docs/adr/0144 D2 and D5, as read in the first round; and for this delta scripts/pm/clause2-line.mjs (`readClause2Line`), scripts/pm/record-recognisers.mjs (`reviewFace`), scripts/check-adr-0087-registration.mjs (`breakingDeclaration`, `readDisposition`, `findMigrationPrescription`) (all read in the live tree, none reviewed)

### ① Derived judgments

- **The head moved by one commit that touches one file.** `git diff 0bbcdd99..f9675566` is `.changeset/31949-currency-field-repointed.md` alone (+4/−2). `packages/metadata-protocol/src/protocol-write-face.ts`, `packages/objectql/src/protocol-destructive-currency-mode.test.ts` and `content/docs/data-modeling/currency.mdx` are byte-identical to the first-round head, and the merge base is unchanged (`0cd594b3`). Every ① judgment of record 6749733592 therefore stands on this head as written: the accept set narrowed by exactly one transition, no row read, `force` inherited whole, one new wire value `currency_field_repointed`, the `currency_mode_to_record` message byte-identical, the message's claims true of the live tree, eleven cases pinning it.
- **No new accept-set or public-surface change.** The delta is a changeset body: one declaration line respelled, one HTML comment added, one sentence of prose corrected. It publishes nothing the first-round head did not.

### ② Semver level

- **`Clause-②:` line: the must-fix is fixed.** The changeset and the PR body both carry `Clause-②: no (narrowing) — a save that answered 200 now answers 409 without `force``, verbatim from claim amend 1. `readClause2Line` reads `{ kind: 'declared', value: 'no', arm: 'narrowing' }` on each. `reviewFace` on the four committed paths with both texts as `declaredOn` answers `face: 'narrowing'`, `tierName: 'CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER'`, `hits` empty. Its reason is true of the tree: the diff touches no file under `packages/spec`, adds, removes or renames no key, export or type, and the same save with `force` is accepted as before (pinned by the harness's `force` case and by `protocol-save.ts` skipping the whole gate on `request.force`). `objectstack migrate meta` has nothing to rewrite. ### ③ Boundary flags

- **Face and tier now agree.** The recogniser derives the narrowing face at CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER on this head, the tier this review was served at. The first record's flag that `Served-tier` would not stand on the derived face is closed.
- **Check-runs on `f9675566`:** 57 runs, 39 `success`, 17 `skipped`, 1 `cancelled`, 0 failed. The cancelled run is `PR-body guards (claim · duplicate · Part-of · single-writer path)` at 19:49:38Z; a later run of the same check completed `success` at 19:49:59Z and supersedes it (the body edit re-triggered the workflow). `Check Changeset` ×2, `Lint & Repo Gates`, `Governed Surface Queue Guard`, `Test Core` 1–8 and its aggregate, `Build Core`, `Build Docs` and the type-check families are all `success`.
- **Dogfood battery: escalated to the seat, not a contract finding.** The `(narrowing)` arm makes one full dogfood run on the final head owed (`.claude/agents/os-dev.md`; the seat's review checklist reworks a PR whose `dogfood_battery` is missing or not pinned to the head). The only os-dev report on the card (6747960601) reads `dogfood_battery: n/a`, written when the arm read null, and no later report exists on either thread. The PR body's sentence "its reading is in the os-dev report on the card" is therefore not true of the card as read at 20:17Z. The CI `Dogfood Regression Gate` is `success` on this head with its shard matrix `skipped`, so it is no substitute reading. This is a pre-queue obligation of the dev and the seat, outside what this record judges: the seat confirms a `dogfood_battery` line pinned to `f9675566` before the queue. A card comment moves no head.
- **`adr_note`:** unchanged. ADR-0144 D5 (or D2) owes a dated note naming `currency_field_repointed`; the seat files the follow-up card (Tier H). Not blocking.
- **`out_of_scope_findings`:** unchanged, carrier #31911.

### ④ Design judgment

- **The narrowing itself is unchanged from the first-round head and its judgment stands:** it takes no declared capability away at the consumer (the save still lands with `?force=true` on the REST door and every declaration still parses), and the spec on `main` states no refusal it would be making real; it is one more finding in the existing destructive gate, in the family of `field_type_change` and `currency_mode_to_record`. The eight attempts to break it in record 6749733592 apply to byte-identical source.
- **First-round nit 1 (changeset named `PUT /meta`, Studio and a package publish as doors taking `force`): fixed.** The parenthetical is gone and the sentence now reads "Re-submit with `?force=true` on `PUT /api/v1/meta/:type/:name` to save", the one door that reads `force`, matching the docs page.
- **First-round nit 2 (recompute named for a path target with `homeAmount` reports `code_blank` until #31911): stands,** accepted deviation with carrier #31911, no edit.
